en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
16. The Mansion of Sirimā “Your horses are yoked, supremely adorned, powerful, swift,
yet with heads cast down as they gallop toward the abyss.”
And five hundred chariots created by supernormal power follow you,
with horses urged on by charioteers.
You stand there, adorned, upon that excellent chariot.
Illuminating like a flame or a fire,
O Anomadassi of exquisite form, I ask you:
why did you approach the Supreme One with your body?
“The deities, having fashioned it again and again, delight in that which is called the unsurpassed attainment of the summit of sensual pleasures;
from that body, a nymph of lovely form [arises].”
"Have you come here to pay homage to the Supreme One?
What good deeds did you perform in the past,
by what merit do you now dwell in happiness with immeasurable wealth?"
Your superpowers are unsurpassed, like those of birds in flight;
your radiance shines throughout the ten directions.
You are surrounded by devas and are held in high honor.
“From where have you passed away, O deity, to reach such a happy destination?
Whose instruction do you follow and carry out?
Tell me this, if you are indeed a disciple of the Buddha.”
“In a most excellently constructed city within the forest,
there were female attendants for the illustrious and noble king;
they were supremely well-trained in dance and song.”
In Rājagaha, they announced me as Sirimāti.
But the Buddha, the leader, the bull among seers,
taught me the arising, suffering, and impermanence.
The unconditioned, the eternal cessation of suffering,
and this straight, direct, and auspicious path—
having heard of this deathless state, the unconditioned, I...
In the teaching of the Tathāgata,
the best of those who possess the Dharma, I was perfectly restrained in the precepts and established in the Dhamma taught by the Buddha, the supreme among men.
Having known the stainless state, the unconditioned,
taught by the Tathāgata with his own authority,
right there I attained the concentration of tranquility.
That itself became for me the supreme certainty.
Having attained the distinguished, excellent Nectar,
I was made certain regarding the realization and distinguished myself.
Without doubt, I am honored by many people as I experience no small amount of pleasure and delight.
Thus I am a deity in the realm of the Deathless.
She is a disciple of the Tathāgata, the Best of Men;
seeing the Dhamma, she is established in the first fruit.
Having entered the stream, she shall never again experience a state of woe.
I approached to pay homage to the supreme Anādhivara and to the pleasing monks who delight in wholesome deeds;
I came to revere that auspicious assembly of ascetics.
Full of reverence for the illustrious Dhamma-king,
they were delighted at heart upon seeing the Sage,
the Tathāgata, the supreme man and charioteer of those to be tamed.
“I revere the Guide, who cuts off craving,
who delights in the wholesome, and who is compassionate for our supreme welfare.
The *Sirimā-vimāna*, the sixteenth.
